strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing task selection efficiency in LLM reinforcement finetuning with clear practical importance
Principled Bayesian framework with sound theoretical foundation (Proposition 1 shows update rules preserve Beta family)
Lightweight interpolation-based implicit evidence mechanism with negligible overhead (<0.2%) that doesn't require extra rollouts
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 3 domains, 2 model sizes, with thorough ablations on λ and ρ demonstrating clear design principles
Effective visualizations (heatmaps in Figs. 7-8, ETR curves) clearly showing how BOTS shifts computation from trivial/unsolvable to informative tasks
Natural extensibility to exponential family distributions (Appendix E.4.1) showing generality of framework
Practical applicability with low computational overhead and reasonable hyperparameter guidance
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: combines standard techniques (Bayesian inference, Thompson sampling, Beta-Bernoulli models) without profound new insights; main innovation is linear interpolation between reference models, which is relatively simple

Questionable assumptions underlying implicit evidence: (1) linear interpolation assumes linear relationship between global capability and per-task success, (2) μ_t estimated on biased batch causes overestimation of true global capability (acknowledged but not thoroughly validated), (3) reference model choice critical but treated ad-hoc without systematic ablation

Marginal empirical improvements in many settings (e.g., Math-1.5B TTB=0.64, 36% acceleration is useful but not transformative); BOTS-DOTS (implicit evidence only) often matches or exceeds full BOTS, undermining claimed value of combining evidence sources, especially for larger models

Hyperparameter sensitivity: two critical parameters (λ, ρ) require tuning with domain-dependent optima; no principled procedure for selecting these given new tasks; different training stages benefit from different values (acknowledged but unresolved)

Limited experimental scope: only binary rewards (extensions outlined but unvalidated), single RL algorithm (GRPO only), small models (1.5B, 7B), single dataset family (GURU), single model family (Qwen); generalization claims are overstated

Weak baseline comparisons: BOTS-MoPPS and BOTS-DOTS are constructed ablations rather than full implementations of cited methods (Qu et al., Sun et al.); missing experimental comparisons to recent online selection methods despite extensive citations

Distributional shift bias in capability estimation unresolved: quality of implicit evidence noticeably degrades for larger models in later training stages (F.2) but root cause not investigated; F.3 shows Thompson sampling is not critical to performance, questioning its importance
No statistical rigor: single runs without confidence intervals or error bars; some results marked with '-' (target never reached) complicating comparison; unknown variance across random seeds

strengths: Well-motivated practical problem addressing task selection efficiency in LLM RFT
Clean Bayesian framework with intuitive posterior update rule incorporating multiple evidence sources
Lightweight interpolation-based implicit evidence requiring no additional rollouts
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple domains and model scales with thorough ablations
Consistent empirical improvements (36% speedup in math domain) and strong BOTS-DOTS baseline validation
weaknesses: Limited novelty: primarily combines known techniques (Beta-Bernoulli posteriors, Thompson sampling, explicit/implicit evidence from prior work) with Propositions 1-2 being standard Bayesian conjugacy results
Modest and inconsistent empirical gains with BOTS-DOTS frequently competitive or superior (undermining explicit evidence motivation) and narrowing improvements on 7B models

Critical hyperparameter sensitivity (λ, ρ) without principled selection; default settings appear arbitrary despite authors acknowledging stage-dependent optima but declining to propose adaptive schemes

Implicit evidence has fundamental limitations: depends on reference model choice, becomes unreliable late training (Figure 5), selection bias from adaptive batch B_t, linear interpolation assumptions unvalidated, poor extrapolation guidance
Severely limited scope: binary rewards only, single RL algorithm (GRPO), three specific domains, Qwen models only; unclear generalization to RLHF, preference learning, or other settings

Weak baseline comparisons: BOTS-MoPPS is reduced Chen et al., BOTS-DOTS is 'proxy inspired by DOTS' (not direct), offline baseline simplistic, missing comparisons with recent dynamic curriculum methods

Missing critical ablations: no variants of interpolation method tested empirically (kernel methods discussed but not compared), no systematic reference model sensitivity analysis, Thompson sampling necessity not justified

Presentation issues: key limitations downplayed, BOTS-DOTS competitiveness contradicts motivation, negative results (implicit evidence degradation) minimized, 34-page manuscript with important ablations in appendix

strengths: Well-motivated practical problem: clearly articulates inefficiency of uniform task sampling in RFT and establishes strong motivation for adaptive selection
Principled Bayesian framework: grounded in sound inference with rigorous proofs (Propositions 1-2), Beta-Bernoulli conjugate model, and natural extension to exponential families

Key insight on evidence complementarity: identifies that explicit evidence is stable but sparse early (cold-start), while implicit evidence is dense but unreliable later; tunable fusion parameters elegantly capture this trade-off
Lightweight practical instantiation: interpolation-based implicit evidence requires no extra rollouts, uses pre-computed reference models (standard practice), and adds negligible overhead (≤0.2%)

Comprehensive experimental validation: consistent improvements across 3 domains and 2 model scales (36% acceleration on Math-1.5B, 50% on Logic-7B); well-designed metrics (ETR, TTB, BSF); thorough ablations; informative visualizations showing BOTS shifts computation from trivial/impossible tasks toward informative mid-range
Reproducibility: extensive implementation details, within-framework baselines enabling fair comparison, and promised code release
Honest discussion of limitations and future directions in appendices
weaknesses: Limited theoretical justification for linear interpolation plugin (Eq. 5): no rigorous analysis of when/why linear assumption holds; distributional shift bias (capability estimated on adaptively-chosen batch, not uniform pool) only briefly addressed

Reference model dependency: implicit evidence effectiveness hinges on choosing suitable weak/strong references; unclear how practitioners should select these in new settings; upfront cost of evaluating 2 reference models × 16 rollouts on 77.5k tasks not thoroughly discussed

Hyperparameter selection lacks principled guidance: default λ=0.1, ρ=0.1 appear domain-tuned; paper acknowledges different values work best at different stages yet proposes fixed parameters; no guidance for new domains

Mixed empirical results undermine evidence fusion necessity: Code domain shows BOTS-DOTS matches/exceeds BOTS on several metrics; Logic-7B shows small differences without statistical significance testing; modest improvements (1-5% BSF) lack error bars
Implicit evidence estimator degrades significantly over time: Figure 5 shows ROC AUC approaches 0.5 (random) for 7B by end of training, limiting utility when explicit evidence also sparse
Limited scope: only binary rewards; single dataset (GURU) and model family (Qwen); short training windows (70-100 steps) don't establish persistence of benefits over longer horizons

Incomplete baseline comparisons: BOTS-MoPPS and BOTS-DOTS are within-framework ablations; DOTS additionally uses trajectory replay (not implemented); limited side-by-side comparison to other recent methods
No error bars or significance testing despite RL stochasticity, making modest improvements difficult to assess statistically
Thompson sampling utility function under-justified: why is |p̂^k - p*| optimal? Why is p*=0.5 universal?
